problem: Preserve a small binary-semantic payload using scheduled Chat and lightweight repository transport with zero optional monthly quota and zero incremental cost.

consumer_requirement_classes: raw binary artifact at a consumer-visible path
assumptions.current_chat_repository_mutation_surface: UTF-8 text create/update with stable-path lookup and blob-SHA reconciliation

candidates.mechanism: RFC4648 uppercase base16 UTF-8 chunks; each chunk's content address is b16:<data>; ordered manifest defines payload
candidates.conflict_duplication_risk: low: immutable chunk paths plus manifest CAS; canonical uppercase form removes case aliases
candidates.integration_cost: low: two characters per octet, no padding, simple finite checker
candidates.storage_overhead: 2 text characters per payload octet before JSON framing

candidates.mechanism: RFC4648 base64 UTF-8 chunks with canonical pad bits/padding and strict alphabet
candidates.conflict_duplication_risk: low with immutable chunks/CAS, but canonicalization and chunk-boundary rules add failure modes
candidates.storage_overhead: 4 characters per 3 octets asymptotically before JSON framing

candidates.mechanism: write arbitrary non-UTF-8 bytes directly as repository file
candidates.expected_completion_time: unavailable on current exposed mutation contract
candidates.optional_monthly_quota_fragility: not acceptable if solved via artifact/LFS/package/cloud quota

candidates.mechanism: store binary through hosted artifact/LFS/package/cloud mechanism
candidates.optional_monthly_quota_fragility: fails root zero-quota acceptance because route can depend on finite hosted allowance

candidates.mechanism: preserve text then require user/external process to decode it into binary

selection.why: For a tiny payload it minimizes semantic ambiguity and checker complexity at the cost of 2x textual expansion; it can be verified entirely as bounded text state. Base64 saves storage but adds canonicalization/padding complexity that is not valuable at this scale.

boundary: A canonical text representation can satisfy exact semantic byte preservation. It does not satisfy a materially stronger outcome requiring a raw binary file to exist unless Chat exposes a binary-write/materialization capability; treating the decoder handoff as solved would violate the root policy.
